newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Afghan refugees want to stay in Turkmenistan, IFRC.
newsitem.headline: Afghan refugees want to stay in Turkmenistan, IFRC.

text.p: The Red Cross said on Monday thousands of Afghan refugees who fled last week want to remain in neighbouring Turkmenistan despite safe-conduct guarantees by the Islamic Taleban militia.
"The Taleban want them to return," Bob McKerrow, head of the Almaty-based regional mission of the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, told Reuters.
"But the refugees are digging in their toes, they don't want to move back at this time," he said.
McKerrow said about 8,000 Afghan refugees, not 9,000 as earlier reported by the Red Cross, fled to Turkmenistan from northern Afghanistan following clashes in the region last week.
The forces of Uzbek General Abdul Malik are fighting in northern Afghanistan against the Taleban, who control most of the country, including Kabul.
The Taleban are battling to regain control of territories in the north they briefly won and then lost to the anti-Taleban alliance in May.
McKerrow said his agency and Turkmen officials met Taleban representatives who crossed the border on Monday.
"They guaranteed the safety of refugees if they want to return to Afghanistan," McKerrow said.
He said the Red Cross, United Nations agencies and the Turkmen government were settling the refugees in temporary camps in the desert near Turkmenistan's eastern border town of Takhta Bazar.

The former Soviet republics neighbouring Afghanistan have voiced concern that fighting there could trigger an exodus of civilians. The refugees at Takhta Bazar are the first major influx of Afghan refugees to one of the Central Asian states.
